title: Relational Data Modeling
outcome: Translate TaskFlow business relationships into a relational model that can enforce membership, ordering, labels, comments, ownership, and lifecycle rules.
artifact: A complete Prisma/ER model for TaskFlow core entities with keys, relation tables, uniqueness, and important indexes.
labSteps: List TaskFlow nouns and separate entities from attributes and events.
Model workspace membership as an explicit relation carrying role/state rather than an array on User.
Model boards/lists/tasks and decide which parent IDs should be required.
Model labels through a join table and explain composite uniqueness.
Add comments and timestamps with intentional delete behavior.
Seed a small realistic graph and query it from several directions to validate the model.
failureModes: JSON arrays replacing relational join tables without reason
Using nullable foreign keys where the domain requires ownership
mastery: Can identify invariants enforced by constraints
Can query the model from parent and child directions
commands: pnpm exec prisma migrate dev --name taskflow-core-model
principles: Normalize relationships enough to preserve correctness before optimizing for convenience.
Choose cardinality intentionally: one-to-one, one-to-many, and many-to-many model different business rules.
Use unique constraints and foreign keys to encode invariants where the database can enforce them.
Design TaskFlow entities around actual workflows such as workspaces, members, boards, lists, tasks, comments, and labels.
